drivingQuestion: What is the status of dedicated property before and after it is handed over to the priest?
outcomeNote: A single cited baraita expanding the mishna's ruling; no objection is raised in this unit.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֶרְמֵי כֹהֲנִים אֵין לָהֶן פִּדְיוֹן וְנִותָּנִין לַכֹּהֵן. חֲרָמִים כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן בְּבֵית בְּעָלִים הֲרֵי הֵן כְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״. נְתָנָן לְכֹהֵן — הֲרֵי הֵן לְכׇל דִּבְרֵיהֶן כְּחוּלִּין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לְךָ יִהְיֶה״.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «The Sages taught: Dedications» of property for «priests have no redemption, and one gives» the property «to the priest.» With regard to these «dedications, as long as they» remain «in the house of the owner they are» considered «like consecrated» property «in every sense, as it is stated: “Every dedicated item is most sacred to the Lord”» (Leviticus 27:28). Once the owner «has given them to the priest they are in every sense like non-sacred» property, «as it is stated: “Everything dedicated in Israel shall be yours”» (Numbers 18:14), i.e., it shall be like all other regular property belonging to a priest, which is non-sacred.

moves.summary: a baraita is brought on the mishna's ruling that dedications for priests have no redemption
moves.about: opening the gemara with a baraita on the status of dedicated property before and after it reaches the priest
